name: Standard Project Structure
authorization: User explicitly requested adoption in this chat on 2026-10-10.

core.principle: Some files are shared across projects; technical equivalents vary by technology.

items.purpose: Project purpose, concise scope, setup, execution and verification.
items.applicability: Every project that will be maintained.

items.purpose: Rules for local, generated or sensitive files excluded from Git.
items.applicability: Every Git project, adapted to its technology.
Every project; location depends on technology.

items.purpose: Tests and how to verify the core task.
items.applicability: Every project, proportionate to its risk and size.

items.purpose: Working rules for coding agents and actual project commands.
items.applicability: Recommended for projects developed with agents.

items.purpose: Names and safe examples of required environment variables.
Checks to run when code changes.
items.applicability: Recommended for regularly developed and maintained projects.

dependency_management.goal: The libraries required by a project should be clear when it is opened on another computer.

npm_application_example.version_control_policy: Official npm guidance specifies keeping the lockfile in the source repository.

dependency_management.other_ecosystems: Follow the package manager's appropriate approach for application or library projects.
dependency_management.standardization_rule: Required dependencies must be explicit; filenames can vary by technology.

essential_questions: Whose problem does this project solve, and what is that problem?
How is it installed and run?
Which files contain the feature I want to change?
How do I verify it works and that I have not broken anything?
How are settings, access permissions and data managed?
How is it published, and how is a faulty release rolled back?

dimensions.name: Product information
dimensions.benefit: Reduces drift from the intended purpose during development.

dimensions.name: Code organization
dimensions.benefit: Makes it easier to locate where a change belongs.

dimensions.name: Working practices
dimensions.benefit: Makes resuming a project and handing over work easier.

structure_goals.design_rule: Adding folders is not inherently useful. Each section must have an actual responsibility.

documentation_sections.heading: Project identity
documentation_sections.question: What are its identity, product line and owner?

documentation_sections.heading: Scope
documentation_sections.question: What is being completed now, and what is deferred?

documentation_sections.heading: Requirements
documentation_sections.question: Which tools and versions are required?

documentation_sections.heading: Setup and run
documentation_sections.question: How is it installed and run?

documentation_sections.heading: Configuration
documentation_sections.question: Which settings are required, and where are they supplied?

documentation_sections.heading: Verification
documentation_sections.question: How are tests and other checks run?

documentation_sections.heading: Project links
documentation_sections.question: Where are the authoritative task, design and detailed-documentation locations?

technology_profiles.principle: Projects can share responsibilities while using different technical locations.

profiles.name: Web application
profiles.source_and_project_layout: The framework's layout for pages, source and static files.

profiles.name: Native iOS application
profiles.source_and_project_layout: Project, application and test targets generated by Xcode.
profiles.note: Apple's project creation flow generates configuration and source files for the selected application type. Preserve the natural layout as a starting point.

profiles.name: Python application or packaged automation
profiles.source_and_project_layout: Layout appropriate to the packaging and dependency tools.
profiles.note: A src layout can be useful but has implications such as an installation step during development. A small script and a distributable Python package need not share the same structure.

profiles.name: Very small script
profiles.source_and_project_layout: One entrypoint and only necessary helper files.

reproducibility.goal: A person opening the project should not have to guess how to set it up or verify it.

operations.name: Setup
operations.expected_result: Required dependencies and tools are prepared.

operations.name: Run
operations.expected_result: The application opens in the development environment.

operations.name: Code checks
operations.expected_result: Relevant formatting, static analysis and type checks run.

operations.name: Test
operations.expected_result: Meaningful behavior checks for the product run.

operations.name: Packaging or build
operations.expected_result: The application is prepared for its target environment.

reproducibility.command_rule: Command names vary across technologies. README must contain the actual project commands.

recommendations: Include variable names, explanations and safe example values in .env.example.
Supply actual secrets through the appropriate server or deployment environment.
Use synthetic or appropriately anonymized test data.
Do not accumulate client documents, production database copies or working logs in the source repository.
State which data environment development and testing connect to.

supporting_principles.statement: Separating configuration from code is a core Twelve-Factor principle.
Manage the lifecycle and access controls of secrets separately.

nextjs_public_environment_caveat.statement: Writing a value in .env does not guarantee secrecy. In Next.js, NEXT_PUBLIC_ values can be embedded in JavaScript sent to the browser.

recommended_checks.question: Does the requested user task work?
Were documents updated when setup or usage changed?
Were known gaps and checks that could not run clearly documented?

definition_of_done.distinction: Having a tests/ directory differs from having meaningful tests actually run and pass.
definition_of_done.execution_status: These are suggested review questions; they were not executed against a software project as part of importing the standard.

principles.repository_strategy: Repository boundaries are a separate decision. A shared standard does not require combining every project into one repository.

migration.starting_principle: First identify gaps in the existing structure of working projects.

steps.title: Try one project
steps.action: Use a project selected for development or actively maintained.
steps.constraint: Do not turn standardization into a large parallel project of its own.

steps.title: Record the current state
steps.action: Verify how the project runs, its entrypoints, existing checks and release method.

steps.title: Complete missing working information
steps.action: Align README, required configuration examples and agent instructions with current reality.

steps.title: Choose a concrete structural problem
steps.action: Define the purpose of the change clearly.
examples: Task-related code is hard to find.
Setup cannot be reproduced on another computer.

steps.title: Split necessary moves into small steps
steps.action: After moving a module, check import paths, tests, builds and affected user flows.
steps.constraint: Combining folder changes with major dependency updates or new features makes review harder.

steps.title: Apply useful rules to other projects
steps.action: Do not spread a rule that provided no benefit in the first project across the portfolio. Briefly document technology-appropriate exceptions.

exceptions: Domain folders retained; no web framework or artificial src layout introduced.
translation_note: English translation of the adopted standard; source_sha256 identifies the original supplied document.
